title: Evaluating the Impact of Extended Kalman Filter Odometry on the Performance of 2D LiDAR SLAM Algorithms
content: Accurate localization and mapping are essential for autonomous mobile robots operating in unknown environments. This study investigates the impact of Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-based sensor fusion on the performance of three widely used two-dimensional (2D) LiDAR Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms: GMapping, Karto SLAM, and SLAM Toolbox. Wheel encoder and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data were fused using an EKF and evaluated over multiple trajectories of varying complexity. Localization accuracy was assessed using the Absolute Pose Error (APE) root mean square error (RMSE), while mapping performance was evaluated through occupancy map comparisons. EKF-filtered odometry reduced localization error by 60–75%. Karto SLAM and SLAM Toolbox achieved an additional 13–14% improvement in localization accuracy, whereas GMapping showed only marginal improvement. These results demonstrate that the benefits of sensor fusion depend on the selected SLAM algorithm and trajectory characteristics, providing practical guidance for selecting localization strategies in autonomous mobile robots.
